# The Messy Parents Collection
> The things you're googling at 3am, answered in three minutes — by parents who were googling them last week.
Short, practical guides to the first two years, written by two parents from the
questions they actually asked. Not medical advice; each guide says plainly when
to contact a doctor. Full detail is in the HTML pages listed below — this file
is a convenience index, not a substitute for them.
## About
- [About us](https://themessyparentscollection.com/about.html): who writes these and what they are not.
- [How these guides happen](https://themessyparentscollection.com/editorial.html): sourcing, review and corrections.
- [All guides](https://themessyparentscollection.com/guides.html)
## Guides
### Feeding

- [Why is my baby drinking less milk?](https://themessyparentscollection.com/guides/drinking-less-milk/): A temporary dip is often distraction, teething or a cold; wet nappies, energy and the pattern across the day matter more than one feed.
- [How do I start solids without losing my mind?](https://themessyparentscollection.com/guides/starting-solids/): Start with small, safe tastes when your baby seems ready, and expect practice and mess rather than a proper meal.
- [Why is my baby suddenly refusing the bottle?](https://themessyparentscollection.com/guides/bottle-refusal/): Check the flow, temperature, position and sore mouth—but yes, sometimes your baby has simply rejected that bottle.
- [Is my baby’s spit-up reflux or something else?](https://themessyparentscollection.com/guides/reflux-or-spit-up/): Comfortable spit-up is often harmless; pain, feeding trouble or poor growth deserves a conversation with your baby’s doctor or nurse.
- [Why did my baby spit up hours after a feed?](https://themessyparentscollection.com/guides/spit-up-while-asleep/): Spit-up can appear well after a feed because milk moves slowly through a tiny stomach; how your baby seems matters more than the clock.
- [Why does my newborn want milk again so soon?](https://themessyparentscollection.com/guides/feeding-on-demand/): Wanting milk again soon can be normal, especially during cluster feeding, but feeding plans for premature or medically monitored babies come first.
- [Do I time the next feed from the start or end of the last one?](https://themessyparentscollection.com/guides/timing-feeds-start-or-finish/): We counted from the start of one feed to the start of the next, but our baby’s own feeding plan always came first.
- [Is it normal for a newborn to lose weight after birth?](https://themessyparentscollection.com/guides/newborn-weight-loss/): Some early weight loss is expected; the important part is whether weight begins turning around and your baby is feeding and producing wet nappies.
- [When does the milk actually come in?](https://themessyparentscollection.com/guides/when-does-milk-come-in/): Colostrum is thick, yellow and measured in drops, and that's exactly right. Fuller volume usually turns up between days two and five, often later after a caesarean.
- [How often should I pump around the clock?](https://themessyparentscollection.com/guides/pumping-schedule/): Early pumping often means frequent sessions across day and night; writing down the real times made it much easier for us to manage.
- [Why has my milk supply dropped on one side?](https://themessyparentscollection.com/guides/milk-supply-dropped/): Sides are rarely equal and supply follows demand, so missed sessions are the usual culprit. Heat, pain, a hard lump or feeling flu-like is a different conversation.
- [Is this a blocked milk duct or mastitis?](https://themessyparentscollection.com/guides/blocked-duct-or-mastitis/): A tender area without fever may be inflammation; redness, worsening pain or flu-like symptoms are reasons to seek same-day advice.
- [How long can expressed milk sit out?](https://themessyparentscollection.com/guides/storing-expressed-milk/): Fresh breast milk can keep for up to four days in a cold home fridge, but NICU rules may be much shorter—ours used a 24-hour limit.
- [How do I keep expressed milk ready when we are out?](https://themessyparentscollection.com/guides/warming-milk-out-and-about/): Take it cold and warm it when she's ready. Holding milk at 37 degrees for hours is the thing to avoid, and a microwave is never the answer.
- [How long should I sterilise baby bottles?](https://themessyparentscollection.com/guides/sterilising-baby-bottles/): Wash feeding equipment first, then sterilise it. UK guidance continues to twelve months, while a premature baby may be given stricter rules.
- [How much milk should my baby have?](https://themessyparentscollection.com/guides/how-much-should-she-eat/): Around 150–200ml per kilo per day is a general guide after the first week. Wet nappies, growth and your baby’s cues matter more than one feed.
- [How can I tell how much milk my breastfed baby is getting?](https://themessyparentscollection.com/guides/how-much-from-the-breast/): You cannot measure it directly, so watch the useful signs: wet nappies, swallowing and weekly weight. Feed length tells you very little.
- [Why does my baby always seem hungry?](https://themessyparentscollection.com/guides/constantly-hungry/): Frequent feeding is normal and rarely means underfeeding. Check the nappies and the weekly weight before adding more milk — and burp her before deciding.
- [Why does my baby drink too fast and then vomit?](https://themessyparentscollection.com/guides/feeding-too-fast/): Hold the bottle more horizontally, sit her upright, and pause deliberately every ten to fifteen sucks. Pacing beats any slow-flow teat.
- [What is cluster feeding?](https://themessyparentscollection.com/guides/cluster-feeding/): Feeds bunched together, usually in the evening. Normal, exhausting, and not evidence that your milk has run out.
- [Which baby formula is best?](https://themessyparentscollection.com/guides/choosing-a-formula/): First infant formulas meet the same regulated standard, so choose on availability and how she takes it. Specialist formulas are a medical decision, not a shopping one.
- [How do I move from breast milk to formula?](https://themessyparentscollection.com/guides/breast-milk-to-formula/): Replace one feed at a time and wait several days before the next. Two to three weeks is comfortable for her and for you.
- [Does breastfeeding for three months still count?](https://themessyparentscollection.com/guides/how-long-does-breast-milk-matter/): Breastfeeding for three months still counts. Every week adds something, and stopping before six months does not erase what you have already done.
- [How do I stop pumping without it hurting?](https://themessyparentscollection.com/guides/weaning-off-pumping/): Drop one session at a time, hold for several days, and express just enough for comfort in between. Stopping abruptly is what causes blocked ducts.
- [How do I make up a formula bottle safely?](https://themessyparentscollection.com/guides/making-up-formula/): Powder isn't sterile, which is why water temperature matters. Fresh for each feed is safest — and check what your machine actually does rather than assuming.
- [What changes when my baby starts formula?](https://themessyparentscollection.com/guides/formula-side-effects/): Firmer nappies, more gas and longer gaps between feeds are common while she adjusts. Rash, swelling or blood is a different matter.

### Sleeping

- [Why won't my baby nap?](https://themessyparentscollection.com/guides/wont-nap/): Nap trouble is often a timing problem: too early and they are not tired, too late and they are overtired.
- [Is this sleep regression?](https://themessyparentscollection.com/guides/sleep-regression/): It may be a sleep change or a new skill, and there can be several of these—not just one famous regression.
- [Why is my baby waking at 5am?](https://themessyparentscollection.com/guides/early-waking/): Early waking is often linked to light, bedtime or the last nap, though some babies really are tiny morning roosters.
- [Why is my newborn awake all night and asleep all day?](https://themessyparentscollection.com/guides/day-night-confusion/): Newborns need time to learn day from night; morning light, quiet nights and shared shifts can make the wait easier.
- [Where should my newborn sleep?](https://themessyparentscollection.com/guides/safe-sleep-newborn/): The safest place is on their back, on a firm, flat, completely clear sleep surface, for every sleep.
- [Why is my newborn so noisy while sleeping?](https://themessyparentscollection.com/guides/newborn-noises-at-night/): Newborn sleep can be astonishingly loud; we learned to notice breathing effort and colour rather than reacting to every grunt or squeak.
- [Why does my baby sleep with their mouth open?](https://themessyparentscollection.com/guides/sleeping-with-mouth-open/): An open mouth during sleep can follow mild congestion, but persistent mouth breathing is worth mentioning to your baby’s doctor or nurse.
- [Should I wake my baby to change a wet nappy?](https://themessyparentscollection.com/guides/nappy-changes-at-night/): We usually left a comfortable sleeping baby in a wet nappy until the next feed, but changed a poo nappy, a leaking nappy or one irritating sore skin sooner.
- [Should I swaddle my baby or let them kick?](https://themessyparentscollection.com/guides/swaddling/): Swaddling may help sleep and free kicking builds strength. Keep hips loose, avoid overheating and stop swaddling at the first signs of rolling.
- [How much should my baby be sleeping?](https://themessyparentscollection.com/guides/how-much-sleep-newborn/): Most newborns sleep for about fourteen to seventeen hours across the whole day. Count naps too, and look at feeding, wet nappies and alertness rather than chasing one exact number.
- [Why won't my baby sleep? Is she just not tired?](https://themessyparentscollection.com/guides/she-wont-sleep-at-all/): A baby who will not settle is often overtired, not wide awake. Try starting earlier, keeping the room dark and handing over before you reach your limit.
- [Could my baby's nappy be stopping her from settling?](https://themessyparentscollection.com/guides/it-was-the-nappy/): Check the simple physical things first: the nappy, seams, labels, temperature and even a hair around a toe. Sometimes the smallest thing is the whole problem.
- [How can I put my sleeping baby down without waking her?](https://themessyparentscollection.com/guides/putting-her-down-awake/): Wait until her arms feel heavy, lower her bottom and feet first, then keep a hand on her chest for a moment. The transfer is often the hardest part.
- [Why does my baby suddenly open her eyes while sleeping?](https://themessyparentscollection.com/guides/she-wakes-herself-up/): This is usually the startle reflex or a normal change between sleep cycles. A safe swaddle in the early months and waiting a moment can help.
- [My baby slept for six hours. Should I have woken her?](https://themessyparentscollection.com/guides/six-hour-stretch/): If she is feeding and growing well and is past the early weeks, a long sleep is usually a gift. If she has a feeding plan, follow that instead.
- [Why does my baby nap briefly but sleep for hours at night?](https://themessyparentscollection.com/guides/short-naps-long-nights/): Night sleep often lengthens before daytime naps do. A forty-minute nap can be one complete sleep cycle, even when it feels far too short.
- [Why does my baby sleep through every noise?](https://themessyparentscollection.com/guides/sleeping-through-noise/): Newborns can sleep through an impressive amount of noise, but that often changes. Steady background sound is easier to live with than trying to keep the whole house silent.
- [My baby won't wake up. When should I worry?](https://themessyparentscollection.com/guides/when-to-worry-she-wont-wake/): A long sleep can be fine if she wakes fully and feeds well. If she is hard to wake, floppy, pale or missing feeds, get medical help now.
- [When will my baby sleep through the night?](https://themessyparentscollection.com/guides/when-do-they-sleep-through/): Longer stretches arrive slowly, not on one magic date. When people say a baby sleeps through, they often mean five or six hours, not the whole night.
- [For a premature baby, does sleep or feeding matter more?](https://themessyparentscollection.com/guides/sleep-and-the-premature-baby/): In the early weeks, feeding comes first and you may need to wake her. Use corrected age and follow the plan from your baby's doctor or NICU nurse.
- [Does my baby need a sleep schedule?](https://themessyparentscollection.com/guides/building-a-sleep-schedule/): Do not force a strict clock. Notice the pattern she is already making, keep the order familiar and let the times move as she grows.
- [Is it okay to take my baby for a walk at night?](https://themessyparentscollection.com/guides/night-walks-with-the-pram/): A night walk is usually fine and can help her settle. Keep the pram uncovered, dress her for the weather and move her to a flat sleep surface when you get home.
- [My baby has slept most of today. Is that okay?](https://themessyparentscollection.com/guides/sleeping-more-than-usual/): One sleepy day can be normal if she still feeds well and is bright when awake. Sleepiness with poor feeding or difficulty waking needs medical advice.

### Development

- [When will my baby roll, sit and crawl?](https://themessyparentscollection.com/guides/rolling-sitting-crawling/): Milestone ranges are wide and the order varies, so look for steady progress rather than a perfect month on a chart.
- [When should my baby babble, point and say first words?](https://themessyparentscollection.com/guides/first-words/): Communication starts with sounds, looks and gestures long before clear words, and all of your baby’s languages count.
- [Do newborn babies blink less than adults?](https://themessyparentscollection.com/guides/newborns-and-blinking/): Newborns really do blink less than adults, so the long stare can be ordinary; the appearance and movement of the eyes matter more.
- [Was that a real baby smile or just wind?](https://themessyparentscollection.com/guides/is-that-a-real-smile/): Early smiles are often spontaneous; social smiles usually arrive later, and corrected age matters for babies born early.
- [When will my baby hold their head up?](https://themessyparentscollection.com/guides/head-control/): Head control builds over months, not overnight. Corrected age matters for milestones after an early birth, but tummy time still starts gently from the beginning.
- [Why does my baby get sleepy during feeds?](https://themessyparentscollection.com/guides/growth-spurt-signs/): Sleepier but alert when awake and feeding well is usually growth. Sleepy plus feeding badly is the combination that gets checked.
- [Is my baby gaining enough weight?](https://themessyparentscollection.com/guides/weight-gain-per-day/): Daily gain is mostly noise — weigh weekly, same scales, and watch the direction. Rates slowing as she grows is expected, not a warning.
- [Why does my baby keep putting her hands in her mouth?](https://themessyparentscollection.com/guides/hands-to-mouth/): Hands to mouth and interlaced fingers is her mapping her own body, and it's a real step. Sucking hands isn't always hunger. Persistent one-sided movement or a hand that stays fisted past a few months is worth raising at her next check.
- [Why don't my baby's eyes move together yet?](https://themessyparentscollection.com/guides/eyes-dont-coordinate/): Eyes drifting or crossing in the early months is common and usually settles by around four months corrected. A turn that's constant, or a white reflex in the pupil, needs seeing rather than waiting.
- [Is camera flash safe for my baby's eyes?](https://themessyparentscollection.com/guides/flash-photos-and-her-eyes/): A few flashes at normal distance are not thought to cause harm — she'll dislike it rather than be damaged by it. Keep the camera back, and use daylight where you can.
- [When should I start playing with my newborn?](https://themessyparentscollection.com/guides/when-to-start-playing/): Play starts immediately and it's mostly your face and voice at close range. Short bursts, stop when she looks away, and count from her due date if she was early.
- [How long should I wait after a feed before tummy time?](https://themessyparentscollection.com/guides/tummy-time-after-eating/): There is no exact timer. Wait until she seems comfortable after a feed. If she spits up easily, give her longer or try before the next feed.
- [Why does my baby's head control seem worse?](https://themessyparentscollection.com/guides/head-tilt-in-tummy-time/): Uneven progress is normal and a heavier head makes it look like going backwards. Always tilting to the same side, or a neck that resists turning, is worth raising at her next check.
- [When do babies start laughing?](https://themessyparentscollection.com/guides/first-laugh/): Usually around three to four months corrected, often at an object rather than a person. No laugh by around six months corrected, alongside little eye contact or response to your voice, is worth raising at her next check.
- [When do babies start talking?](https://themessyparentscollection.com/guides/when-do-babies-talk/): Cooing from around two months, babbling from around six, words often near a year — all corrected if she was early. No babbling by nine months corrected, or little response to your voice, is worth raising at her next check.
- [Why does my baby roll one way but not the other?](https://themessyparentscollection.com/guides/rolling-back-to-tummy/): Back to tummy usually comes first and the return roll can take weeks more. Once she rolls at all, the swaddle stops and the cot stays empty — she'll roll in her sleep before she can roll back.
- [Do I need to teach my baby to sit?](https://themessyparentscollection.com/guides/learning-to-sit/): She works it out herself — floor time and opportunity are what you provide. Not sitting unsupported by around nine months corrected is worth raising at her next check.
- [Why does my baby favour one hand?](https://themessyparentscollection.com/guides/hand-preference/): A mild preference can happen, but she should still use both hands. A strong, consistent preference before eighteen months is worth raising at her next check.
- [What can I do with my three-month-old?](https://themessyparentscollection.com/guides/playing-with-a-three-month-old/): Short bursts, heavy repetition, and following what she's already interested in. Stop when she looks away — pushing through it makes the next hour harder.
- [Which baby toys are actually worth buying?](https://themessyparentscollection.com/guides/choosing-toys/): Simple, open-ended and a little ahead of where she is. Rotate a small set rather than filling the floor, and check everything for parts small enough to swallow.
- [When will my baby play independently?](https://themessyparentscollection.com/guides/independent-play/): A few minutes from around four to six months, lengthening through the year. Stay nearby, don't interrupt when she's absorbed, and put fewer toys out rather than more.

### Health

- [Is teething making my baby miserable?](https://themessyparentscollection.com/guides/teething/): Drool, chewing and sore gums can be teething; fever or a baby who seems unwell needs another explanation.
- [What should I know about my baby’s first fever?](https://themessyparentscollection.com/guides/first-fever/): Your baby’s age and how they look matter as much as the number, so a young baby with fever needs quick medical advice.
- [Why won’t my baby’s nappy rash clear up?](https://themessyparentscollection.com/guides/nappy-rash/): Simple nappy rash often improves with gentle cleaning, dry skin and barrier cream; spreading or persistent rash needs checking.
- [Are newborn hiccups normal?](https://themessyparentscollection.com/guides/newborn-hiccups/): Newborn hiccups are very common and usually bother parents more than babies; a comfortable baby can still be put down to sleep.
- [How do you unblock a newborn's nose?](https://themessyparentscollection.com/guides/blocked-nose-newborn/): Saline before feeds and humidity at night helped Ari. We never used suction ourselves, although gentle suction is another option parents may be shown.
- [Why did milk come out of my baby's nose?](https://themessyparentscollection.com/guides/milk-from-the-nose/): Milk can sometimes travel through a baby's nose during spit-up; it looks frightening, but a baby who recovers quickly is often fine.
- [Why does my newborn breathe fast and then slow down?](https://themessyparentscollection.com/guides/fast-breathing-newborn/): Brief changes between faster and slower breathing can happen in newborns; breathing effort, colour changes or pauses mean calling your baby’s doctor or nurse.
- [Why did my newborn's body shake for a second?](https://themessyparentscollection.com/guides/newborn-trembles-and-jerks/): Brief trembling or sleep jerks can happen in newborns, but repeated movements or a baby who seems unwell should be checked.
- [What do the different NICU stages mean?](https://themessyparentscollection.com/guides/nicu-stages/): The stage number describes how much support she needs right now, not how she's doing overall — and units number them differently, so ask what yours mean.
- [Why does the incubator show such a low temperature?](https://themessyparentscollection.com/guides/incubator-temperature/): A low-looking number may be the incubator setting rather than your baby’s temperature, so ask the NICU nurse or doctor what it measures.
- [Is there a minimum weight before she can come home?](https://themessyparentscollection.com/guides/nicu-discharge/): Discharge usually depends more on stable breathing, temperature and feeding than one magic weight, but each NICU has its own criteria.
- [Why can my premature baby only manage a little milk?](https://themessyparentscollection.com/guides/preemie-feeding-stamina/): Premature babies often tire before finishing a feed, but a clear drop, colour change or breathing change needs the NICU nurse or doctor.
- [Why is my premature baby’s tummy firm and bloated?](https://themessyparentscollection.com/guides/preemie-bloated-tummy/): A firm, swollen tummy in a premature or small baby needs quick medical advice, especially with green vomit, blood or colour changes.
- [What is corrected age and when should I use it?](https://themessyparentscollection.com/guides/corrected-age/): Count milestones from the due date rather than the birthday. Vaccinations usually follow actual age, so check which age each appointment is using.
- [Which growth chart should a premature baby use?](https://themessyparentscollection.com/guides/preemie-growth-charts/): Percentiles mean little without the right chart and corrected age. Watch her own line over weeks — direction beats position every time.
- [When can I take my newborn out?](https://themessyparentscollection.com/guides/newborn-immune-and-going-out/): There is no magic waiting date; your baby’s health and the type of outing matter more, especially after a premature birth.
- [What colour should my baby’s poo be?](https://themessyparentscollection.com/guides/newborn-poo-colours/): Mustard yellow and seedy is the classic, but yellow, orange, brown and green can all be normal. White, red or black needs checking.
- [How long can a baby go without pooing?](https://themessyparentscollection.com/guides/baby-not-pooping/): A gap alone is not constipation. If the poo is soft when it arrives, wet nappies continue and your baby seems well, waiting is often enough.
- [Why does my baby cry every evening?](https://themessyparentscollection.com/guides/colic-and-witching-hour/): Predictable evening crying can be common and still be awful. Movement and less stimulation may help; if you are at your limit, put baby down safely and step away.
- [Why does my baby have so much wind?](https://themessyparentscollection.com/guides/wind-and-gas/): Wind is usually swallowed air plus a gut still learning its job. Stopping partway through and slowing the feed helped us; a firm swollen tummy is different.
- [Do colic drops actually help?](https://themessyparentscollection.com/guides/colic-drops/): Colic drops help some babies and do very little for others. Try one thing at a time, follow the product instructions and keep tea or water out of a young baby’s milk.
- [What are the little bumps on my newborn’s face?](https://themessyparentscollection.com/guides/newborn-skin-bumps/): Milia and newborn acne are common and usually clear by themselves. A non-fading rash, blisters or any rash with fever is different.
- [How can I tell if my newborn is actually in pain?](https://themessyparentscollection.com/guides/is-my-baby-in-pain/): Groaning, fidgeting and throat clearing can all happen in normal newborn sleep. Watch colour, breathing and whether the sound is truly different.
- [Is my baby too hot, and is air conditioning safe?](https://themessyparentscollection.com/guides/is-baby-too-hot/): Check the chest or back of the neck, not cool hands and feet. Air conditioning is fine when it keeps the room comfortable and does not blow directly on baby.
- [Will sleeping with the head to one side cause a flat head?](https://themessyparentscollection.com/guides/flat-head/): Flat spots are common and often improve. Vary pressure while baby is awake, but safe sleep stays unchanged: on the back, flat and with nothing added to the cot.
- [How long do vaccine side effects last in babies?](https://themessyparentscollection.com/guides/baby-vaccine-side-effects/): A grumpy day or two, sleepiness and a sore injection site can be expected. Repeated vomiting, dehydration or a baby who is difficult to wake needs advice.
- [Is my baby’s big round tummy normal?](https://themessyparentscollection.com/guides/overfed-big-tummy/): Round and soft after a feed is ordinary baby shape. Firm, tight or shiny—especially with vomiting, pain or unusual sleepiness—needs checking.
- [Is it normal for my baby not to poo after switching to formula?](https://themessyparentscollection.com/guides/formula-and-constipation/): Longer gaps are expected when switching. Soft when it arrives, a soft tummy, and plenty of wet nappies means waiting is reasonable — but get your limit from your own doctor.
- [Why was my baby’s vomit yellow?](https://themessyparentscollection.com/guides/yellow-vomit/): Creamy curdled milk can look pale yellow. True yellow, yellow-green or green vomit, blood or repeated forceful vomiting needs urgent medical advice.
- [What should I do when my baby has her first cold?](https://themessyparentscollection.com/guides/her-first-cold/): Most baby colds need comfort, saline and time. Watch her breathing, feeding and wet nappies more closely than the amount of mucus.
- [Is 37.2°C or 37.7°C a fever in a baby?](https://themessyparentscollection.com/guides/a-slightly-raised-temperature/): A fever is 38°C or higher. If she is under three months, that needs urgent medical advice even if she otherwise seems well.
- [Does anti-reflux milk help with reflux?](https://themessyparentscollection.com/guides/anti-reflux-milk/): Anti-reflux milk is thicker milk, not medicine. It may reduce spit-up, but use it only as directed and check that the teat still flows comfortably.
- [What should I ask about my baby's reflux medicine?](https://themessyparentscollection.com/guides/reflux-medicine/): Ask what the medicine is treating, how long the trial lasts, when it will be reviewed and whether the dose changes as she grows.
- [Could my baby's milk be causing bloating or discomfort?](https://themessyparentscollection.com/guides/could-it-be-the-milk/): Bloating is often swallowed air or an immature gut. Before changing milk, ask what is being tested and how you will know whether it helped.
- [Why are small bumps spreading across my baby's body?](https://themessyparentscollection.com/guides/bumps-on-her-body/): Take one clear photo each day and notice how she is behaving. A rash that does not fade under pressure needs urgent medical help.
- [Will the marks from the NICU fade?](https://themessyparentscollection.com/guides/marks-from-the-nicu/): Most NICU marks fade slowly over weeks or months. Keep the skin comfortable, protect it from strong sun and compare monthly rather than daily.
- [Why does my baby have sticky or itchy eyes?](https://themessyparentscollection.com/guides/itchy-eyes/): A sticky, watery eye with no redness is often a blocked tear duct. A red eye, swollen lid or redness spreading onto the face needs medical advice.
- [What if I forget my baby's vitamin D or iron drops?](https://themessyparentscollection.com/guides/vitamin-d-and-iron-drops/): After missed drops, restart the usual dose unless your baby's doctor or nurse says otherwise. Never double up to catch up.
- [How do I give medicine to my baby?](https://themessyparentscollection.com/guides/giving-her-medicine/): Use the correct syringe, keep her upright and give small amounts into the side of her cheek. Ask before mixing medicine into milk.
- [Do premature babies follow the normal vaccine schedule?](https://themessyparentscollection.com/guides/vaccines-and-a-premature-baby/): Routine vaccines usually follow actual age, not corrected age. Ask your baby's doctor about the schedule, side effects and RSV protection.
- [Is my baby choking or just gagging?](https://themessyparentscollection.com/guides/is-she-choking/): Gagging and coughing are noisy. Choking may be silent. If she cannot breathe, cry or cough, treat it as an emergency and call for help.
- [How long should I wait after a flight before seeing my baby?](https://themessyparentscollection.com/guides/coming-home-from-a-flight/): There is no single safe waiting period after a flight. Ask your baby's doctor, then focus on illness, handwashing and sensible distance.
- [What should I do after my baby bumps her head?](https://themessyparentscollection.com/guides/a-small-fall-or-bump/): After a head bump, note the height, surface and time. Watch how she behaves, and get urgent help for serious warning signs.
- [What should I take when my baby needs to go to hospital?](https://themessyparentscollection.com/guides/going-to-hospital/): Take one phone note with her weight, medicines and symptoms. At hospital, ask what is being checked, what would reassure them and when it will be reviewed.

### Parent Sanity

- [Is it normal to feel like I can’t handle one more person touching me?](https://themessyparentscollection.com/guides/touched-out/): Wanting twenty minutes without anybody touching you does not make you a bad parent; it means you need a real break.
- [How do we split the nights so nobody breaks?](https://themessyparentscollection.com/guides/splitting-nights/): Protected sleep shifts usually help more than both parents waking for everything, even if the split is not perfectly equal.
- [How do we manage visitors after the baby arrives?](https://themessyparentscollection.com/guides/visitors/): Decide your visitor rules before the doorbell rings, then keep the message short, kind and firm.
- [Is it normal not to feel an instant bond with my baby?](https://themessyparentscollection.com/guides/father-not-feeling-it/): An instant rush of love is not the only way bonding begins; it can grow through ordinary care, time and getting to know your baby.
- [Is it normal to regret having a baby sometimes?](https://themessyparentscollection.com/guides/overwhelmed-new-parent/): Overload can produce thoughts like this without making them true. Say it to one person early; persistent numbness, hopelessness or thoughts of harm need help.
- [What does months of broken sleep do to parents?](https://themessyparentscollection.com/guides/parent-sleep-deprivation/): Broken sleep can affect your mood and judgement before you notice it. Protected blocks of sleep, taking turns and asking for help matter.
- [Why am I caring for my baby but not enjoying it?](https://themessyparentscollection.com/guides/checklist-mode/): Being on duty for months flattens enjoyment, and it's usually a workload problem rather than a feelings one. Persistent low mood, numbness or hopelessness is worth a doctor's appointment — don't leave it.
- [Why am I exhausted even though I have help?](https://themessyparentscollection.com/guides/tired-even-with-help/): Having help does not switch off the mental load. What often helps most is a block of time when you are truly off duty.
- [Why can't I sleep when someone else has the baby?](https://themessyparentscollection.com/guides/awake-when-you-could-be-sleeping/): Your body may be resting while your mind stays on watch. Regular off-duty nights and a calmer sleep routine can help it relearn how to switch off.
- [Can I love my baby and still resent how hard this is?](https://themessyparentscollection.com/guides/loving-her-and-resenting-it/): You can love your baby and still resent how relentless parenting feels. The thought does not cancel the love or make you a bad parent.
- [Is it wrong to need a proper break from my baby?](https://themessyparentscollection.com/guides/i-need-a-proper-break/): Needing a proper break is not a failure. Ask for a clear block of time before you reach the point where everything feels unbearable.
- [What if bonding with my baby still hasn't clicked?](https://themessyparentscollection.com/guides/still-feels-like-meh/): Bonding can grow slowly through feeding, holding and showing up each day. It does not have to arrive as one huge feeling.
- [Does holding my sleeping baby count as bonding?](https://themessyparentscollection.com/guides/are-we-bonding-if-shes-asleep/): Yes. Holding her while she sleeps can be warm, familiar bonding time, as long as you stay awake and keep her sleep space safe.
- [Does having a baby ever get easier?](https://themessyparentscollection.com/guides/does-it-get-easier/): It changes more than it simply gets easier. Sleep, communication and confidence often improve, even while new problems appear.
- [What should I agree before hiring overnight help?](https://themessyparentscollection.com/guides/hiring-night-help/): Agree the hours, duties, settling, medicines and morning handover in writing before the first overnight shift.
- [How do I explain our baby-care rules to someone helping?](https://themessyparentscollection.com/guides/briefing-whoever-helps/): Write the important rules down once, keep them specific and explain why they matter. Clear instructions are kinder than weeks of corrections.
- [How do I let a nanny or night nurse go?](https://themessyparentscollection.com/guides/letting-help-go/): You do not need proof of wrongdoing to end an arrangement that no longer feels right. Keep the conversation calm, short and fair.
- [How do I find childcare help without an agency?](https://themessyparentscollection.com/guides/finding-help-without-an-agency/): Try several agencies and local parent recommendations, then check references yourself and use a paid trial before making anything permanent.
- [Why is travelling with a baby so stressful?](https://themessyparentscollection.com/guides/travelling-with-her/): Most parents find baby travel stressful. Plan the feed, sleep and airport questions early, then expect the routine to wobble for a few days.
- [Is it bad to use my phone while my baby sleeps on me?](https://themessyparentscollection.com/guides/your-phone-in-her-room/): Using your phone while she sleeps is not the same as giving her screen time. The useful question is whether it keeps pulling you away when she is awake.
- [What do I really need for a few hours out of the house with my baby?](https://themessyparentscollection.com/guides/an-hour-out-with-her/): For a short outing, pack for the likely problems rather than every possible disaster. A small bag makes leaving home much easier.
- [Why are we arguing so much since having a baby?](https://themessyparentscollection.com/guides/the-fights-about-her/): More arguments after a baby are common because both parents are tired and stretched. Talk about the load in daylight, not during the 3am explosion.
